children.name: Minquartia guianensis Aubl.
children.description: A tree with white latex growing to ~20 m, known as black manwood or huambula (family Olacaceae/Coulaceae). Its native range spans Central and South tropical America from Honduras to Brazil, growing primarily in the wet tropical biome. It yields very hard, durable timber, is used medicinally and for food, and is a source of the rare fatty acid minquartynoic acid. IUCN: Near Threatened.

children.name: Coula edulis Baill.
children.description: The sole species of the monotypic genus Coula (family Olacaceae/Coulaceae), an evergreen tree 25-38 m tall with a dense deep-shading crown and alternate simple leaves 10-30 cm long. Native to western and west-central tropical Africa from Guinea to the DR Congo, it grows in lowland rainforest; its drupes are 3-4 cm long with an extremely hard shell and an edible oil-rich kernel (the African walnut or Gabon nut). IUCN: Least Concern.
